title: GPU nodegroup lifecycle module for Private VPC (ASG + Karpenter hybrid)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Create a reusable Terraform module that manages GPU-capable node groups for Private (VPC) deployments supporting both ASG-backed nodegroups and Karpenter provisioners in a hybrid, upgrade-safe way. The module should codify launch template/AMI versioning, instance type families (on-demand/spot), taints/tolerations, node labels, and integrated health checks that surface node GPU readiness and driver state to the Redwood Console. This aims to reduce manual patching, simplify OS/driver upgrades, and provide a consistent rollout/rollback story across customer VPCs.

Background & Motivation:
- Private customers run latency-sensitive and regulated workloads on GPU-backed nodes. Upgrades and autoscaling must be predictable and observable.
- Current ad-hoc TF modules and scripts make upgrades risky (e.g., driver mismatch, stale kubelet flags) and complicate support.
- We need a canonical module that supports: ASG-based reserved pools, Karpenter for burst/spot capacity, graceful drain/replace semantics, and health checks that block unhealthy nodes from serving traffic.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
1) Terraform module API that allows customers to define: preferred instance families, capacity type mapping (ONDEMAND/SPOT), GPU driver bake strategy (AMI vs. user-data install), and labeling/taint policies.
2) Module works in two modes: "managed-asg" (creates ASG + launch template) and "karpenter-provisioner" (creates provisioner CR via Terraform kubernetes provider).
3) Rolling upgrade path: support blue/green AMI swaps for ASG and provisioner-level pod eviction strategy for Karpenter; zero-downtime rollouts for critical pods (via PodDisruptionBudgets and top-off logic).
4) Health checks: node considered healthy only when kubelet Ready, NVIDIA device plugin Ready, nvidia-smi returns expected driver version, and kube-proxy is Ready. The module exposes a null_resource check that can be integrated into CI/CD for pre-promote gating.
5) Observability: emit node health events to Console (via cluster-side controller or prom-to-forwarder) and surface per-node GPU-ready metric for routing decisions.
6) Backwards compatibility: existing Private clusters using our older launch template naming must be supported; provide a migration plan and automatic tagging to opt into the new module.

Design notes / decisions made so far:
- AMI strategy: prefer baked AMIs (driver + runtime) for customers with strict image policies. Fall back to user-data/DaemonSet installer when customers request latest driver at boot. Module parameter: "gpu_image_strategy" = ["AMI", "DaemonSet"].
- Karpenter mapping: map capacityType->instanceLifecycle. Add provisioner taints for lower-priority (spot) nodes so critical workloads schedule only on reserved ASG.
- Health check implementation: two-layer checks:
  1) infra-level health (Terraform null_resource invoking kubectl to verify Node conditions and a small job that runs "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader" on node via DaemonSet).
  2) runtime-level readiness exported to Prometheus metrics (node_gpu_driver_ok metric).
- Upgrade strategy: for ASG, use launch template version pinning + set desired_capacity + rolling_update via Auto Scaling Group instances replacement with lifecycle hooks that run kubelet drain and finalize. For Karpenter, create a short-lived provisioner with new constraints and cordon old nodes via a controller and allow scale-down. Provide Terraform helper scripts for staged rollout.
- Taints/labels: provide module inputs for default taints (e.g., gpu=true:NoSchedule) and standard labels (redwood.io/node-pool, redwood.io/gpu-family).
- Security: credentials for image registries and KMS integration documented; module will not embed secrets (use SSM/KMS-provided ARNs).

Testing & Validation Plan:
- Unit tests for TF module using terratest harness (ginkgo) in CI, mocking provider calls where possible.
- Integration canary in our Private staging: deploy 1 ASG pool and 1 Karpenter provisioner in a sandbox VPC, run GPU workload e2e (inference batch + container warmup) and assert no request errors during rolling replace.
- Soak tests: leave new nodes under load for 72h to catch driver memory leaks.
- Healthcheck gate: add a pre-merge pipeline job that runs the Terraform null_resource checks against a disposable cluster and fails on any node failing the GPU readiness check.

Rollout / Migration Plan:
1) Publish module in our private Terraform registry under redwood-private/gpu-node-lifecycle.
2) Announce to SE/ES teams with migration guide and automated tagger script that labels existing ASGs for replacement.
3) Run migration in two phases per-customer: create ASG + new launch template in parallel, drain old nodes using lifecycle hooks, and monitor GPU-ready metric.
4) Provide a one-click rollback: reapply old launch template version and set ASG desired_capacity to previous size; for Karpenter, delete new provisioner and uncordon nodes.

Open questions / Risks:
- Driver install time variance on spot instances may cause long startup times; need thresholds to treat nodes as unschedulable until driver probe passes.
- Some customers require on-prem air-gapped images; ensure DaemonSet installer supports local tarball install.
- Terraform kubernetes_provider race when creating provisioner CR vs. cluster being ready. We may need a small operator or k8s_job with retries instead of direct CR creation.

Deliverables / PRs to open:
- TF module code (module root + examples) — repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git (WIP branch: feat/gpu-lifecycle-module)
- Terratest suite and CI pipeline change that runs null_resource checks.
- Migration helper script (python) that tags ASGs and creates a dry-run plan.

Acceptance test checklist (to close ticket):
- [ ] Module published to private registry with docs and example for ASG and Karpenter modes.
- [ ] CI Terratest passes and null_resource health check added to pipeline.
- [ ] Successful canary migration in staging cluster with zero 5xx observed during rollout.
- [ ] Upgrade and rollback runbooks documented and reviewed by SRE.

Estimated follow-ups (future tickets):
- Add driver auto-rollback if node fails health checks n times in a row.
- Cost-optimization guide to pick instance families based on workload profile.
